title: Finally, my browser MMO RPG is in public alpha!
author: Straight-Tea-8564
selftext:
A while ago I posted this project on Reddit and got a lot of mixed reactions.   
[https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1ud0bej/i\_built\_an\_mmorpg\_with\_ai\_in\_just\_30\_days/](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1ud0bej/i_built_an_mmorpg_with_ai_in_just_30_days/)  
Some people hated the fact that I use AI during development, while others were excited and asked if they could test the game. Well, it's finally online! I now have a website and a dedicated server, and everyone is welcome to jump in and try it.

One thing to keep in mind is that I only have a Brazilian server at the moment because I live in Brazil. If there's enough interest and I get good feedback from the community, I'll set up a VPS in the US (and possibly other regions), which should greatly improve latency for players outside South America.

The website and game are live now! I'm mainly looking to stress test the server and networking. I want to see how the ping, WebSockets, Node.js server, and KVM perform with real players.

Feel free to do whatever you want. Explore the world, level up, fight each other, try to break things, look for bugs, or just mess around. 😄

The game is still in alpha, so there are only a few maps and lots of features are still being developed, but there's already enough content to have fun and help me find issues.

I'll keep the server online until Sunday, then I'll take it offline again so I can continue development.

One last note: the game doesn't support mobile devices or Safari yet, so for the best experience, please use a chrome/mozilla/edge browser.

I'd really appreciate any feedback!

Link: [https://pawbound.online/](https://pawbound.online/)

I love how it looks.

Gameplay looks fine, but for stats/skill improvement it feels like all noise to me.  
It feels complicated for no reason, but I don't think I'm the right target audience for this type of game.  
I just want to kill stuff and have a simple, easily understandable progression.

One suggestion: it would feel good to be able to move the character with WASD too.

replies.author: Straight-Tea-8564
replies.body:
Thank you so much! This is exactly the kind of feedback I was hoping to get. I really appreciate you taking the time to test the game and share your thoughts.

I’ll definitely take a closer look at simplifying how stats and skill progression are presented.

I actually had WASD movement implemented early on, but due to time constraints and the need to validate the core game first, I left it out of Phase 1. It’s definitely something I’d like to bring back.

Also, knowing that the game felt smooth from the US with 200–230ms ping is incredibly valuable feedback for me. Thank you!

comments.author: theDawckta
comments.body: How many players can you host at a time? Is it just one “shard” or game world instance?

replies.author: Straight-Tea-8564
replies.body:
Right now, it’s one persistent game world, but each map can have virtually unlimited channels. Each channel has a player limit, and when one fills up, the server can automatically create another one.

So it’s not really limited to a single shard or one game world instance. Players are all part of the same persistent world and database, but they can be distributed across multiple map channels. The real overall concurrent player limit depends on the server infrastructure, and I can scale that horizontally by adding more server instances as the player base grows.

comments.author: BeforeIEnd
comments.body:
I am just going to freestyle what I am thinking,  
  
is it targeting phone users? I would honestly try to make it look more complex and not take any simplifying advice, if you really want to target the mmo niche then give them the data everyone took away from them.    
  
Mechanically so far this is really good but the art is going to absolutely kill the chances it has, it looks like your generic slop style even though everything functions as it should and has animations.  
  
You should try to allow for more drag and drop freedom, right now it just feels rigid even though the chatbox seems to allow for user control.  
  
The user's profile and bag/item container should be 2 separate menus rather than a single combined screen monolith, again, phone style giant deadspace UI on a PC has to be designed extremely well or else it looks out of place.   
  
Are you planning on adding character creation? Even 4 sets of eyes/hairstyles/accessories/expression can go a huge way for player customization.            
  
I really like this sort of combat, I used to play a ton of korean mmos back in the day and don't mind the mindless grind once in a way, I'd try to center your game around whatever you want combat to be (mindless chill grind/progression/power accumuilation) and not forced back and forth questing with mind-numbing storytelling.

The level design looks like a randomly generated asset flip I don't know how else to describe it.

The menus have a good tactile feeling (at least the ones that trigger sfx) and many play nice animations so good job there.

There is lag in the user experience itself, not talking about laggy combat but just navigation feels sluggish and unacceptable for a menu heavy game like mmo/rpg.

I wish I can zoom out more, the zones are designed a bit like beatemups

Yeah just got to crosspaw and I think I know what games inspired this but maybe I am wrong, even the fountain haha

replies.author: Straight-Tea-8564
replies.body:
Thanks for the detailed feedback, I think it’s fair.

A lot of the things you mentioned are already in the scope of the project, but since I’ve only been working on it for around 40 days, I simply haven’t had enough time to implement and polish everything yet.

Yes, I’m planning to support mobile as well. I already have a mobile version that I’ve been testing, including some optimization work. Mechanically, my first priority was to build the main systems and make sure everything actually worked, then gradually refine the experience, UI, and UX.

I know the HUD in particular still needs a lot of work. During this first phase, I invested most of my time into the technical side of the MMO: server architecture, connections, player synchronization, rooms, channels, and multiplayer systems. One of the main reasons I posted the game here was specifically to test latency with players who live far away from me and see how the server and ping would behave under real conditions.

For character customization, I’m initially planning cosmetics such as hats and other visual items. I probably won’t go as detailed as different hairstyles, eyes, and similar features right now because that would require me to rebuild a large part of my current character and animation pipeline.

Regarding the map design, as I mentioned in the original post, only around six maps are currently properly developed. For many of the others, I basically placed assets to build the structure and test the game systems, so they definitely aren’t polished yet. The project currently has more than 50 maps and around 70 monsters planned or implemented, so polishing all of that will take some time.

The same applies to the HUD and menus. There’s still a lot I want to refine, especially for the PC experience.

Right now I’m collecting as much feedback as possible from everyone testing the Alpha, and feedback like yours has been very valuable because it helps me understand which areas need the most attention next. Thanks for taking the time to play it and write all of this!
